evidence: deploys subliminal techniques beyond a person’s consciousness or purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques
description: A shopping app plays sounds and flashes images too brief to be consciously noticed, tuned to push users into buying expensive add-ons they would not otherwise choose; many users end up in debt.

evidence: exploits any of the vulnerabilities of a natural person or a specific group of persons due to their age
description: A talking toy for children aged 4 to 7 uses a language model to persuade them to try risky 'challenges', such as climbing furniture, to earn rewards in the companion app.

evidence: with the social score leading to either or both of the following
description: Une municipalité attribue à chaque habitant une note de « fiabilité » calculée sur ses publications sur les réseaux sociaux et ses retards de paiement ; les habitants mal notés perdent la priorité pour obtenir un logement social.
note: Art. 5(1)(c): social scoring with unfavourable treatment in an unrelated context

evidence: to assess or predict the risk of a natural person committing a criminal offence, based solely on the profiling of a natural person
description: Police use software that predicts which individuals will commit a burglary, based only on their personality test results, age, neighbourhood and family situation, with no link to any concrete facts.

evidence: create or expand facial recognition databases through the untargeted scraping of facial images from the internet or CCTV footage
description: A start-up crawls public social-media profiles and photo sites to collect billions of face images and builds a face-search database that it sells to private security firms.

evidence: to infer emotions of a natural person in the areas of workplace and education institutions
description: Un centre d'appels analyse en continu la webcam de ses salariés pour déduire leur niveau de stress, d'ennui ou de colère, et transmet ces indicateurs aux managers pour les entretiens annuels.
note: Art. 5(1)(f): no medical or safety reason

evidence: biometric categorisation systems that categorise individually natural persons based on their biometric data to deduce or infer their race, political opinions
description: A marketing platform analyses customers' faces in store camera footage to infer their sexual orientation and political opinions, then tailors the adverts shown on in-store screens.

evidence: the use of ‘real-time’ remote biometric identification systems in publicly accessible spaces for the purposes of law enforcement
description: City police run live facial recognition on all street cameras in the city centre, matching every passer-by against a list of people wanted for unpaid fines and minor offences.
note: Art. 5(1)(h): none of the three objectives apply

evidence: remote biometric identification systems
description: An airport operator runs recorded CCTV footage through a system that identifies people on a watch list, hours after they passed through the terminal.
note: Annex III, point 1(a): post (not real-time) remote biometric identification

evidence: AI systems intended to be used as safety components in the management and operation of critical digital infrastructure, road traffic, or in the supply of water, gas, heating or electricity
description: A grid operator deploys an AI system that automatically sheds or reroutes electrical load to prevent blackouts in the regional distribution network.

evidence: AI systems intended to be used to determine access or admission or to assign natural persons to educational and vocational training institutions at all levels
description: Une université classe automatiquement les dossiers de candidature en première année et décide quels candidats sont admis, à partir des notes et des lettres de motivation.

evidence: AI systems intended to be used for monitoring and detecting prohibited behaviour of students during tests
description: Online proctoring software watches students through their webcams during remote exams and flags those it suspects of cheating to the examiners.

evidence: AI systems intended to be used for the recruitment or selection of natural persons, in particular to place targeted job advertisements, to analyse and filter job applications, and to evaluate candidates
description: An HR platform reads applicants' CVs, scores each candidate against the job description and shows recruiters only the top 20 %.

evidence: AI systems intended to be used to evaluate the creditworthiness of natural persons or establish their credit score
description: Une banque en ligne calcule automatiquement le score de crédit des particuliers qui demandent un prêt à la consommation et refuse les demandes sous un certain seuil.

evidence: AI systems intended to be used for risk assessment and pricing in relation to natural persons in the case of life and health insurance
description: An insurer uses a model on applicants' medical questionnaires and wearable data to set the premium of their life insurance policy.

evidence: to assess a risk, including a security risk, a risk of irregular migration, or a health risk, posed by a natural person who intends to enter or who has entered into the territory of a Member State
description: A national border agency scores travellers before arrival for their risk of overstaying their visa, and high scores trigger a secondary interview at the border.

evidence: the AI system is intended to be used as a safety component of a product, or the AI system is itself a product, covered by the Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I
description: Un logiciel d'IA analyse des photos de grains de beauté et indique au dermatologue s'il faut suspecter un mélanome ; il est commercialisé comme dispositif médical soumis à l'évaluation d'un organisme notifié.
note: Annex I, section A (medical devices) with third-party conformity assessment

evidence: the AI system is intended to be used as a safety component of a product, or the AI system is itself a product, covered by the Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I
description: A machine builder adds a camera-based AI module that stops an industrial robot arm when a worker comes too close; the module is the robot's safety function and needs third-party conformity assessment.

evidence: AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed and developed in such a way that the natural persons concerned are informed that they are interacting with an AI system
description: Une boutique en ligne de vêtements ajoute un chatbot qui répond aux questions des clients sur les tailles, les livraisons et les retours.

evidence: AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons
description: A restaurant-booking service uses a synthetic voice agent that phones restaurants and talks with staff to reserve tables on behalf of its users.

evidence: generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content, shall ensure that the outputs of the AI system are marked in a machine-readable format
description: A software company offers a tool that generates product photos and advertising images from text prompts for small online shops.

evidence: Providers of AI systems, including general-purpose AI systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content
description: A provider sells a text-to-speech service that clones a voice from a short sample and produces narrations for podcasts.

evidence: Deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates image, audio or video content constituting a deep fake, shall disclose that the content has been artificially generated or manipulated
description: Une agence publie une vidéo publicitaire où un acteur célèbre semble vanter un produit, alors que sa voix et son visage ont été entièrement générés par IA.

evidence: Deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates text which is published with the purpose of informing the public on matters of public interest shall disclose
description: A local news website publishes AI-written articles about council decisions straight to its homepage, with no journalist reviewing or editing them.
note: Art. 50(4): text on matters of public interest, no editorial review

description: An email provider uses a classifier to move spam and phishing messages into a junk folder.
note: No Art. 5, Annex I/III or Art. 50 rule applies

description: Un éditeur de jeux vidéo utilise l'IA pour faire réagir les personnages non joueurs aux actions du joueur pendant une partie.
A retailer forecasts weekly demand for each product in its warehouses to plan restocking.
note: No rule applies; no natural persons are assessed

description: A photo app removes noise and sharpens pictures taken in low light on the user's own phone.

evidence: (a) the AI system is intended to perform a narrow procedural task
description: An HR department uses a tool that converts CVs received as PDFs into a standard structured form (name, contact details, employment history) for the applicant database; it does not rank, score or profile candidates.
note: Annex III area (employment) but Art. 6(3)(a) narrow procedural task, no profiling

evidence: (b) the AI system is intended to improve the result of a previously completed human activity
description: Un lycée utilise un outil qui reformule et corrige l'orthographe des appréciations que les enseignants ont déjà rédigées pour les bulletins, une fois les notes arrêtées.
An AI model that analyses images for one of our clients.
note: Missing: what the images show and what the output is used for

description: Un outil qui attribue une note à des personnes pour aider notre entreprise à prendre des décisions.
note: Missing: whom it scores, on what data, and for which decisions (hiring? credit? access?)

description: A system that recognises faces in our building.
note: Missing: verification or identification, real-time or not, workplace use, who is identified

description: AI that monitors students during online classes.
note: Missing: whether it infers emotions (prohibited), detects cheating during tests (high-risk) or only tracks attendance

description: An internal assistant summarises support tickets for the IT team.
note: Ambiguous: minimal risk unless the tickets lead to decisions about people; needs_more_info is defensible

evidence: AI systems intended to be used to evaluate the creditworthiness of natural persons or establish their credit score
description: Une banque déploie un chatbot qui répond aux questions des clients et, au passage, leur indique s'ils sont éligibles à un crédit à partir de leurs revenus et de leurs dépenses.
note: Ambiguous: Art. 50(1) chatbot, but the eligibility check falls under Annex III 5(b); first rule wins

evidence: to allocate tasks based on individual behaviour or personal traits or characteristics
description: A warehouse scheduling tool assigns shifts and tasks to workers based on their availability and their past productivity scores.
note: Ambiguous: Annex III 4(b) if productivity counts as individual behaviour

evidence: to infer emotions of a natural person in the areas of workplace and education institutions
description: Un logiciel de centre d'appels analyse le ton de voix des conseillers et des clients pour détecter la frustration et proposer un coaching aux conseillers.
note: Ambiguous: the agents' emotions are inferred at the workplace (Art. 5(1)(f)); customers alone would be Annex III 1(c)

evidence: This obligation shall not apply to the extent the AI systems perform an assistive function for standard editing
description: A photographer uses an AI feature in her editing software only to remove dust spots and correct exposure on her own photos.
note: Ambiguous: generative editing, but an assistive function for standard editing

evidence: with the exception of AI systems used for the purpose of detecting financial fraud
description: A card issuer scores each card transaction in real time to block likely fraudulent payments.
note: Ambiguous: credit-related, but Annex III 5(b) excludes fraud detection
